quandoUsar: Show which step of a checkout, sign-up, or setup the user is on, above the content (`horizontal`) or beside it (`vertical`).
Flows where it is possible to go back to a step already done: with `onStepSelect`, completed steps become buttons.
Flag a step that failed, such as a declined card: `error` swaps the number for an alert and the message takes the place of the description.
quandoEvitar: Use `onboarding-checklist` when the steps can be done in any order and checked by hand.
Use `tabs` when the sections are independent and the user can move back and forth between them freely.
Use `adaptive-stepper` to choose a number with minus and plus buttons; despite the similar name, this item indicates steps.

teclado.acao: With `onStepSelect`, move focus between the completed steps and the current one, without wrapping; in right-to-left text, ← and → are swapped.
Moves to the first step or to the current step.
On a completed step, calls `onStepSelect` with its index.

acessibilidade: Without `onStepSelect` it is a read-only `role="group"`; with it, it becomes a `<nav>` of buttons. The current step has `aria-current="step"` and each step has its state in hidden text (“Completed”, “Error”).
An `aria-live="polite"` region announces “Step N of M: label” on each change of `current`, and `completeLabel` at the end; these fixed texts are in English.
Only completed steps enter the `Tab` order; the current and future ones have `aria-disabled`, and the arrow keys also reach the current one.
movimento: On advancing, the line between steps fills with a spring starting from the step that finished; skipping several steps fills one line after another, and the current step's ring appears last.
A completed step's number shrinks and gives way to a drawn checkmark (on an error, an exclamation mark); new descriptions rise with a slight blur and the height follows.
With “reduce motion”, lines, markers, and texts change immediately.
responsivo: The horizontal one measures its own width (container query): below 30 rem it hides the labels, keeps the markers, and shows the current step's label and description underneath; `compact` forces this mode.
With `details="current"`, only the current step shows its description, which saves height; errors always appear.
notasIA: Import from `@/components/ryan-ui/stepper/stepper`. It is controlled by `current`, the index of the step in progress; use `current={steps.length}` to mark the whole flow as completed.
The stepper only indicates: each step's content and the back and continue buttons are up to you, by changing `current`.
To go back to completed steps, pass `onStepSelect={setCurrent}`; only indices lower than `current` fire. The error goes on the step itself, in `steps[i].error`.
